reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is an instructional presentation about creating YouTube chapters and timestamps to help viewers navigate content and potentially improve channel visibility. Its references to views and subscribers concern configuring a YouTube feature, while the presentation qualifies the search-exposure claim and acknowledges that chapters could reduce watch time.

citations.quote: Now video chapters are essentially timestamps that you put in your video description
you need to include a timestamp of zero minutes and zero seconds
Once you have your first zero timestamp created, you can set up the rest of the timestamps however you see fit.
this may actually reduce the watchtime of your videos

opening.argument: The presentation links a low-effort viewer action to a concrete audience-growth return. It instructs creators to add a zero timestamp and then configure additional timestamps, while presenting the result as guaranteed to produce more views and subscribers. The description states the same outcome in unequivocal terms. That is not merely neutral navigation advice: it frames a simple configuration step as the route to acquiring valuable digital audience assets, without establishing that the promised result reliably follows.

citations.quote: you need to include a timestamp of zero minutes and zero seconds
Once you have your first zero timestamp created, you can set up the rest of the timestamps however you see fit.
which is guaranteed to get you more YouTube views and subscribers?
WILL get you more views and subscribers on YouTube.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an instructional presentation does not answer the central problem: the instruction is paired with an asserted guaranteed return. The cited explanation establishes how to enter timestamps, but it does not establish that doing so guarantees views or subscribers. The acknowledgement of possible watch-time reduction actually shows that the presenter is making a consequential growth claim while leaving its reliability unresolved.

citations.quote: Now video chapters are essentially timestamps that you put in your video description
this may actually reduce the watchtime of your videos

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted language should be read in context as a tutorial about a YouTube feature, not as proof of a guaranteed acquisition scheme. The speaker explains that chapters are timestamps in the description and openly says the watch-time effect may be negative. The promotional wording does not show payment, a required purchase, or fraudulent acquisition of money or property; it describes a possible channel-performance benefit from using a platform feature.

citations.quote: Now video chapters are essentially timestamps that you put in your video description
this may actually reduce the watchtime of your videos
we can't directly prove a link between timestamps and video snippets

opening.argument: Several risk signals reinforce the misleading growth pitch. The title promises “MORE SUBSCRIBERS & MORE VIEWS” through a “Simple Trick,” the description says the feature “WILL get you more views and subscribers,” and the narration uses the word “guaranteed.” The same description directs viewers to subscribe, visit a guide, download vidIQ, and use an affiliate program. Together, an easy growth promise and multiple external conversion paths make this look like promotional acquisition of audience assets rather than a carefully bounded educational claim.

citations.quote: How to Get MORE SUBSCRIBERS & MORE VIEWS - Simple Trick!
WILL get you more views and subscribers on YouTube.
which is guaranteed to get you more YouTube views and subscribers?
DOWNLOAD vidIQ FREE
vidIQ AFFILIATE PROGRAM

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes technical instructions but omits the unusually strong certainty and conversion language surrounding them. A disclaimer that chapters might reduce watch time does not neutralize “guaranteed,” “WILL get you,” the “Simple Trick” framing, or the listed download and affiliate pathways. Those signals matter because the issue is not whether timestamps exist, but whether the growth outcome is presented too confidently while viewers are steered toward related promotion.

citations.quote: How to Get MORE SUBSCRIBERS & MORE VIEWS - Simple Trick!
WILL get you more views and subscribers on YouTube.
this may actually reduce the watchtime of your videos

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are ordinary promotional calls to action surrounding a technology tutorial, not evidence of a scam mechanism. The description identifies the topic as creating and using YouTube chapters, and the narration expressly qualifies the search claim: “we can't directly prove a link.” It also acknowledges a possible downside to watch time. Strong marketing language can be excessive without establishing deceptive acquisition, payment, or an inauthentic reward.

opening.argument: Although it adopts the format of creator education, the content functions as a funnel for participation in the channel and its products. It promises that timestamps and chapters can produce more views and subscribers, tells viewers to subscribe for more tips, and supplies links for a free vidIQ download, a full guide, an academy, support, and an affiliate program. The educational wrapper therefore serves a promotional objective: viewers are encouraged to perform a simple setup and expect audience growth, while being directed into the provider’s broader ecosystem.

citations.quote: the YouTube tool, channel and learning academy that educates you on your YouTube journey
Subscribe for more tips just like this
DOWNLOAD vidIQ FREE
LEARN MORE AT THE vidIQ ACADEMY:
vidIQ AFFILIATE PROGRAM

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels the format instructional, but format does not resolve function. The claimed benefit is not just easier navigation; it is more views and subscribers, and the description couples that claim with subscription, download, academy, and affiliate invitations. Explaining where to place timestamps can be genuine, yet the surrounding promises and calls to action still make the presentation promotional and potentially misleading.

citations.quote: This cool feature (that you can see in action below this sentence) WILL get you more views and subscribers on YouTube.
Subscribe for more tips just like this

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The material's promotional elements do not transform the underlying subject into a scam. The speaker gives concrete operational steps: open Creator Studio, select a video, and add chapters using timestamps. The description separately lists resources and social links, while the growth discussion is qualified by an admission that a direct connection to search snippets cannot be proved. That is marketing around education, not evidence that the simple setup extracts money or guarantees a fraudulent return.
